types.tag: Call Type 1: TenneT can receive funding
types.definition: TenneT can receive money from the call: as lead, as a funded partner or as a funded buyer.

types.tag: Call Type 2: TenneT can take part, without a grant for itself
types.definition: TenneT can take part without receiving money, for example as an unfunded or associated partner, a co-funder, a user-committee member, a test-site or data provider, an end user or launching customer, or a peer in a project of other grid operators.

types.tag: Call Type 3: TenneT cannot receive funding, nor take part
types.definition: TenneT cannot take part, but the call touches its field and the funded work would plausibly benefit it through others.

type_1.tag: TenneT can receive funding as Lead of an infrastructure project
type_1.definition: TenneT applies for its own capital project, alone or with another TSO. Example: CEF Energy for cross-border and offshore grid projects, which funds both studies and works. The amounts are large, calls are few and lead times are long.

type_1.tag: TenneT can receive funding as Lead of an innovation project
type_1.definition: TenneT runs a pilot or demonstration and gets part of its own costs funded. Examples are Horizon Europe innovation actions and CETPartnership calls.

type_1.tag: TenneT can receive funding as a funded consortium partner
type_1.definition: TenneT is one of several partners and gets its share at the call’s funding rate. This is the most common case. Funding rates for large companies are often lower, so the grant may cover only part of TenneT’s costs.

type_1.tag: TenneT can receive funding as a funded innovation buyer
type_1.definition: TenneT buys an innovation that doesn’t exist yet, and the funder co-finances the purchase. These are pre-commercial procurement and public procurement of innovation.

type_2.tag: TenneT can take part, without a grant, in a research-led project (universities and institutes)
type_2.definition: Unfunded partner, or a member of the project’s user committee. Co-funder: the company partner often has to contribute cash or in-kind.

type_2.tag: TenneT can take part, without a grant, in a manufacturer-led or startup-led project
type_2.definition: Test-environment or data provider: TenneT offers assets, sites, data or a simulation setting, and the developer gets the grant. End user, problem owner or launching customer: TenneT defines the need and validates the result. For startup instruments like the EIC Accelerator, a customer’s letter of intent strengthens the application. Unfunded system integrator: TenneT fits the developer’s product into its own systems.

type_2.tag: TenneT can take part, without a grant, in a project led by other grid operators (TSOs, DSOs, ENTSO-E)
type_2.definition: These are often about standards, coordination or market design.

type_2.tag: TenneT can support a project led by others (letters, advice, sharing results)
type_2.definition: TenneT backs a project that others lead and receive the grant for, without doing project work itself: it signs a letter of support or intent, sits on an advisory board, or helps share the results. Common when only a single company may apply, as in the EIC Accelerator, or when a supplier develops something TenneT may later buy through its own tenders.

type_3.tag: TenneT cannot receive funding, nor take part, but may benefit from stronger supply-chain capacity for grid equipment
type_3.definition: Support for factories making cables, transformers, converters and HVDC parts. Benefit: shorter lead times and more suppliers.

type_3.tag: TenneT cannot receive funding, nor take part, but may benefit from products it could later buy
type_3.definition: Inspection robots, sensors, grid-enhancing technologies, cable monitoring. Benefit: better offers in future tenders.

type_3.tag: TenneT cannot receive funding, nor take part, but may benefit from flexibility and demand that ease congestion
type_3.definition: Batteries, electrolysers, industrial electrification, flexible loads. Benefit: less congestion, more balancing capacity, better use of connections.

type_3.tag: TenneT cannot receive funding, nor take part, but may benefit from enabling technologies applied to energy (AI, cybersecurity, digital twins)
type_3.definition: AI, cybersecurity, digital twins, data spaces. These only benefit TenneT when applied to energy, so they need the clearest relevance test.

type_3.tag: TenneT cannot receive funding, nor take part, but may benefit from power-system knowledge and future hires
type_3.definition: University research on power systems, materials and offshore engineering. Benefit: knowledge and future hires.

type_3.tag: TenneT cannot receive funding, nor take part, but may benefit from trained technicians and engineers
type_3.definition: Training for technicians and engineers. Benefit: fewer staff shortages.

type_3.tag: TenneT cannot receive funding, nor take part, but may benefit from faster permits and more public support
type_3.definition: Offshore ecology research, nature-inclusive design, local energy projects. Benefit: faster permits and more public acceptance.
